macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: US stocks suffer sharp weekly tech-led losses
items.summary: The S&P 500 fell 1.1% Friday, the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.1%, and the Dow declined 0.3%. Chip stocks weakened further, with Micron down 5.6% and Intel down 5.8%, amid growing concern about the durability of AI-investment returns.[2]

items.title: Fed signals continued focus on price stability
items.summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh avoided giving explicit guidance on upcoming rate decisions but repeatedly emphasized the need to restore price stability. Persistently high inflation is increasing expectations for additional rate hikes in coming months.[2]

items.title: Fed enters blackout period ahead of October meeting
items.summary: The Federal Reserve has entered its pre-FOMC communications blackout before the October 28 policy meeting, leaving upcoming inflation and PMI data and corporate earnings as key market catalysts.[7]

items.title: Inflation remains above expectations
items.summary: September US consumer inflation rose 3.7% year over year, while core inflation increased 2.6%; both exceeded consensus forecasts. Markets are pricing limited odds of an October hike but increasingly expect further tightening later in the year.[1]

items.title: ECB assesses energy-driven inflation risks
items.summary: ECB President Christine Lagarde said elevated eurozone inflation linked to high energy prices has not yet fully affected the broader economy, while officials assess potential second-round effects.[1]

items.title: Tesla unveils new Roadster
items.summary: Tesla unveiled a new Roadster sports car featuring advanced engineering capabilities, including the ability to thrust itself into the air. Tesla earnings are expected to be a major focus for markets in the coming week.[2]

items.title: Meta and Tesla earnings set to dominate the week ahead
items.summary: Investors are preparing for results from Meta and Tesla, with earnings expected to test concerns about elevated AI spending and the sustainability of technology-sector valuations.[1]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin trades above $82,000 amid mixed volatility signals
items.summary: Bitcoin rose roughly 0.2%–0.8% over 24 hours to just above $82,000 in market-data reports. Short-term holders reportedly sent more than 50,000 BTC to exchanges, with about 29,500 BTC moved at a loss, signaling elevated selling pressure despite limited price volatility.

items.title: Crypto liquidations approach $1 billion
items.summary: Nearly $934 million in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated across about 167,400 accounts during the period, with Bitcoin and Ethereum accounting for the largest losses.

items.title: U.S. OCC expected to finalize GENIUS Act rules by October’s end
items.summary: OCC Comptroller Jonathan Gould reportedly said the agency’s final rule implementing the GENIUS Act is expected no later than the end of October, potentially clarifying U.S. stablecoin regulation.

items.title: Russia plans to restrict direct individual crypto P2P trading
items.summary: Updated Bank of Russia guidance says direct individual-to-individual crypto transactions will be permitted only through authorized intermediaries after July 1, 2027. The guidance also bars transfers from digital accounts to self-custodial wallets.

items.title: Latvia adopts crypto tax changes
items.summary: Latvia’s parliament approved amendments extending the investment-account tax regime to crypto assets, generally deferring tax until withdrawals exceed contributions. A one-time 10% declaration mechanism was also reported.

items.title: Polygon releases Bor update fixing denial-of-service vulnerabilities
items.summary: Polygon Labs released Bor v2.10.3 to address two medium-severity denial-of-service vulnerabilities affecting BlockSTM V2 parallel block execution.

items.title: Nine blockchain organizations launch Quantum Alliance
items.summary: A group of nine blockchain organizations formed the Quantum Alliance to establish standards for assessing post-quantum readiness across blockchains, wallets and infrastructure.

items.title: Bitget discontinues services for certain users
items.summary: Bitget announced a one-time discontinuation of services for certain users while saying the broader platform remains operational and affected users’ funds are safe.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Argon
items.summary: Google introduced Gemini 4 Argon for coding, research and professional tasks, with API availability and a combined input-output limit of up to one million tokens. It is also available to eligible Gemini subscribers and in AI Studio Build.[1][2]

items.title: Meta introduces Muse Wonder models
items.summary: Meta announced Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, models designed for AI assistants that retain memory across conversations and work on longer-running goals. The models are available through Meta’s API and Muse Code.[1]

items.title: Black Forest Labs releases FLUX 3 Image Klein
items.summary: Black Forest Labs introduced FLUX 3 Image Klein, an image-generation and editing model with downloadable weights. The 5.6-billion-parameter model is designed to run on a single consumer GPU and supports reference images and spatial placement controls.[1]

items.title: Google reports quantum error-reduction breakthrough
items.summary: Google demonstrated a technique called magic state cultivation on its Willow quantum chip that reportedly reduced errors by about 40 times compared with untreated states. Larger-scale demonstrations are still needed before practical applications.[1]

items.title: Stanford researchers propose faster text generation method
items.summary: Stanford’s Hazy Research introduced Next-Concept Modeling, which generates broad concepts before filling in details. The researchers reported 10-to-31-times faster generation than tested diffusion-based models with comparable or better quality on the reported tasks.[1]

items.title: OpenBMB reports progress on preventing continual-learning forgetting
items.summary: OpenBMB shared a training recipe that mixes filtered model-generated answers into new examples. In the team’s experiments, the approach reduced measured forgetting by 80% to 99% across four models while retaining nearly all new learning gains.[1]

items.title: Microsoft plans expanded use of Maia AI chips
items.summary: Microsoft said its Maia chips are intended to become a primary system for running AI across its products and services. Maia 200 is already serving production workloads including Copilot, while Maia 300 is planned for 2027.[1]

items.title: DeepSeek releases V4.1-Flash-1017 update
items.summary: DeepSeek released a refreshed V4.1-Flash model focused on reasoning, coding, agentic tasks and vision, alongside an expanded search API. Available reporting describes improved benchmark performance and reduced task time and output length.[7][9]

items.title: CERN and Mistral plan a large physics model
items.summary: CERN and Mistral signed a statement of intent to build a foundation model for collider physics, trained on simulated Large Hadron Collider data to support particle reconstruction and identification.[6]

items.title: ByteDance releases OmniHuman 2.0 video model
items.summary: ByteDance made OmniHuman 2.0 available through its BytePlus enterprise platform. The model generates videos from a single image and audio track, with reported durations from 30 seconds to five minutes and a claimed 40% cost reduction.[6]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Xbox announces Xbox Labs for browser-based gaming
items.summary: Microsoft has announced Xbox Labs, a small engineering unit exploring ways to make older-generation games playable in web browsers and distribute games across more devices.

items.title: Epic Games reportedly delays Disney-backed Star Wars and Marvel shooter
items.summary: Epic Games has reportedly delayed its unannounced Disney-backed shooter indefinitely while directing developers toward AI-generated art and broader AI-assisted development workflows.

items.title: Google and Unity announce AI game-development initiatives
items.summary: Google and Unity have announced new experimental AI tools and platforms aimed at helping users create games and assisting developers with production.

items.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 campaign early access begins
items.summary: Early access to the single-player campaign for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has reportedly started.

items.title: The Wolf Among Us Remastered Switch version delayed
items.summary: Telltale has postponed the Nintendo Switch release of The Wolf Among Us Remastered, saying the team needs additional development time.

items.title: Hillthorn announced for November 10 release
items.summary: The card-based detective game Hillthorn is scheduled to launch on November 10 for Nintendo Switch, PC, and mobile devices.

items.title: Street Fighter film opens with $51.1 million worldwide
items.summary: The latest live-action Street Fighter movie reportedly earned $51.1 million globally during its first three days after releasing on October 16.
